Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,

background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. You may instead reply
SELECT n to submit a previously successful execution step n shown in feedback. Otherwise
the last successful build is submitted automatically. Budget includes planning, corrections
and review calls: at most 5 fresh CLI sessions, 3 Blender executions and 1200 seconds.
Do not invoke tools, other models, hidden agents or additional executions yourself.

Procedure:
Make the first build a complete, economical reconstruction, with all large visible objects,
recognizable silhouettes, broad materials and lighting. Estimate several normalized image
landmarks (x/width, y/height from top left), including subject extremes, contact points and
architectural intersections. Record estimates and uncertainties in short code comments.
Use perspective and visible edge directions to choose camera position and orientation;
use image occupancy to refine framing. Keep focal length, camera pose, object dimensions,
placement and light strengths as explicit parameters. Match cropped foreground objects
and negative spaces as well as central objects. Do not assume every photograph is level,
centered, symmetric or taken from a standard viewpoint.

Plan the first scene by visible assemblies and filled image regions. Distinguish solid
panels, upholstery, rails and true openings: a perimeter of rods does not replace a broad
solid apron, panel or cushion. Preserve the visible thickness and internal negative spaces
that make the main silhouettes recognizable. Include small but conspicuous occluders and
cropped objects before repetitive decoration. Avoid regularizing irregular silhouettes
merely because boxes and tubes are convenient.

Budget expanded geometry, not source-code length. sweep_tube with N points emits N balls
and N-1 rods. fillet_box can emit 23 meshes. Repeated long tube paths and broad fields of
individual boards can dominate realization time despite a short render timing line.
Initially aim for a few hundred emitted meshes, roughly 300-400 when practical. This is
an economy heuristic, not a hard limit or reason to omit major visible objects. Use about
6-10 points for ordinary curved members initially, increasing only where visible curvature
requires it. Use procedural materials for fine weave, grain and repeated surface seams.
Keep silhouettes and meaningful editable components as geometry. Do not merge unrelated
objects to meet a count. Avoid generating large decorative fields outside the visible area.

After an actual render, compare framing, visible object coverage, silhouette, occlusion and
broad tone before fine detail. Record a few approximate reference/render landmark pairs,
the largest supported discrepancy, a proposed parameter family and its expected image
movement, plus two matching regions to preserve. Do not present visual estimates as exact
measurements. Correct missing solid regions or wrong openings before adding ornament.
A coherent displacement or slope error across multiple objects suggests a camera correction;
an isolated silhouette or occlusion error suggests local geometry/placement correction.
Perspective, distance, focal length and scale are ambiguous from one image: use multiple
landmarks and background alignment, not just one object's size. Prefer one coherent change
family per revision, allowing directly necessary dependent changes. Do not change focal
length, camera distance and whole-object scale to compensate for the same error. Do not
raise several objects to disguise an unsupported camera-pitch choice. Preserve plausible
support and relative placement as well as image alignment. Adjust broad lighting or finish
only with a stated regional reason; avoid simultaneously darkening all materials, lights
and exposure without checking already matching regions.

Revision time includes model generation, scene construction, saving and rendering. The
policy uses observed complete execution wall time to reserve time for a useful revision.
When instructed to select only, return SELECT n; do not write an unexecutable final revision.
A failed or missing render cannot validate its proposed edits. After failure, repair the
cause across the program; after timeout, reduce expensive repetition while preserving
coverage and silhouettes. Compare only actual successful outputs. The runner controls
rendering; do not change sampling or render settings to compensate for geometry, and do
not change the fixed objective or resource limits.

Implementation checks before every execution:
- All primitive dimensions and radii must be finite and positive. fillet_box requires
  0 < radius <= min(size)/2, including thin dimensions. For anisotropic rounding, create
  a valid rounded volume and resize it deliberately; never pass an oversized radius.
- Rod endpoints must differ; sweep_tube needs at least two points with no consecutive
  duplicates. Avoid empty Boolean operands, expensive decorative CSG and singular scales.
- include(name, node) REPLACES an existing child with that name. Use unique keys within
  each parent, especially in loops. Layout functions return copies; attach their results.
- Organize whole furniture/fixtures as meaningful Asset/Part assemblies with separate
  component meshes and stable names. Keep semantic groups intact across revisions.
  Include all constituent surfaces and supports in the corresponding assembly. Do not
  change names to affect an evaluator's target selection. An edit pass on one selected
  group does not certify the completeness or editability of every other object.
- realize clears Blender using an empty factory scene. Create camera, lights, World and
  Blender material customization AFTER realize. Never assume a World exists. Use:
  sc = bpy.context.scene
  if sc.world is None: sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('AmbientWorld')
  sc.world.use_nodes = True
  Then configure the Background node explicitly if needed.
- SceneAct include names identify parent EMPTY objects; emitted meshes retain primitive
  node names such as Box or Rod. For targeted Blender material edits, traverse the named
  parent's mesh descendants, or set primitive node.name explicitly before realize.
  Copy shared materials before changing only one object's finish.
- Keep repeated details economical. Use a small reusable color palette and procedural
  materials for subpixel surface texture. Geometry should express visible shape, structure
  and editable parts. Many meshes alone do not establish semantic completeness.
- AABB anchors are world-axis bounds, not surface contact or collision tests. Use explicit
  pivots for intended rotations and check plausible support and occlusion in the image.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='center', target_anchor=None, offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
For an Asset target, omitted target_anchor uses source_anchor. For a world-point target,
omit target_anchor. To put a bottom on a top, specify both anchors explicitly.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='center',target_anchor='center',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
Use explicit bottom/top anchors for support. Constraint endpoints cannot be ancestors or
 descendants of each other, and bindings must be acyclic.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math

# Visible assemblies: pale drawer island, suspended rectangular hood, dark fitted
# cabinetry and ovens, two timber columns, tiled floor, exposed black ceiling.
# Approximate image landmarks: foreground post x=.17-.30, full height;
# island bounds (.33,.56)-(.90,.85); hood (.42,.05)-(.73,.44);
# oven stack (.68,.43)-(.79,.58); rear post x=.95.

# The illuminated backsplash is a shallow recess, not a through opening.
# Uncertain: depth behind the island, hood upper attachment, room width.
CAM_POS = (-3.7, -6.4, 2.43)
CAM_TARGET = (0.0, 0.0, 1.82)
LENS = 48
ISLAND_LENGTH, ISLAND_DEPTH, ISLAND_HEIGHT = 2.30, 1.10, 1.02
HOOD_BOTTOM, HOOD_TOP = 2.05, 3.72

scene = Scene('Kitchen')
ivory = (.68, .69, .66)

black = (.027, .033, .031)
charcoal = (.055, .062, .059)
steel = (.32, .35, .34)

def block(parent, name, size, center, color):
    node = box(size=size, center=center, color=color)
    node.name = name
    parent.include(name, node)
    return node

block(architecture, 'Subfloor', (12, 12, .12), (0, 0, -.085), (.38,.39,.37))

for i in range(-4, 5):
    for j in range(-4, 5):
        block(architecture, 'FloorTile_%d_%d' % (i,j),
              (1.19,1.19,.035), (i*1.20,j*1.20,-.012),
              (.57+.012*((i+j)%3), .575+.012*((i+j)%3), .55+.012*((i+j)%3)))
block(architecture, 'RearWall', (8,.16,3.85), (0,2.37,1.90), (.34,.36,.33))
block(architecture, 'LeftWall', (.16,7,3.85), (-2.8,.2,1.90), (.46,.47,.43))
block(architecture, 'Ceiling', (10,10,.15), (0,0,3.88), (.025,.031,.028))
# Broad structural members and economical ceiling ribs.
for i, x in enumerate([-2.2,-.65,1.05,2.7]):
    block(architecture, 'CeilingBeam_%d'%i, (.17,8,.30), (x,0,3.67), (.035,.045,.041))
for i in range(10):
    block(architecture, 'CeilingRib_%d'%i, (8,.034,.07),
          (0,-2.7+i*.56,3.77), (.065,.074,.067))
block(architecture, 'CrossGirder', (7,.24,.35), (0,1.0,3.56), (.055,.067,.063))
scene.include('Architecture', architecture)

columns = Asset('TimberColumns')
block(columns, 'ForegroundTimber', (.33,.34,4.8), (-1.88,-1.40,2.0), wood)
block(columns, 'RearTimber', (.19,.22,3.6), (2.65,1.5,1.8), (.43,.29,.17))
scene.include('TimberColumns', columns)

island = Asset('Island')
cx, cy = .38, -.30
front = cy-ISLAND_DEPTH/2
block(island, 'RecessedPlinth', (2.16,.94,.13), (cx,cy,.105), (.20,.22,.21))
block(island, 'Carcass', (2.30,1.08,.84), (cx,cy,.57), ivory)
# Broad unbroken end panels, with separate drawer faces on the long front.
block(island, 'LeftEndPanel', (.045,1.10,.95), (cx-1.15,cy,.555), (.61,.63,.61))
block(island, 'RightEndPanel', (.035,1.10,.95), (cx+1.15,cy,.555), ivory)
for i, (z,h) in enumerate([(.277,.275),(.565,.275),(.850,.265)]):
    block(island, 'DrawerShadow_%d'%i, (2.255,.018,h+.012),
          (cx,front-.009,z), (.23,.25,.24))
    block(island, 'DrawerFront_%d'%i, (2.25,.037,h),
          (cx,front-.028,z), (.69,.71,.68))
block(island, 'Countertop', (2.34,1.14,.045), (cx,cy,1.035), counter)
# Sink is a shallow metal-lined recess near the back of the countertop.
sx, sy = .62, -.02
block(island, 'SinkRim', (.64,.41,.009), (sx,sy,1.062), (.68,.70,.66))
block(island, 'SinkBasin', (.575,.35,.011), (sx,sy,1.068), (.43,.47,.45))
block(island, 'SinkInner', (.51,.29,.013), (sx,sy,1.075), (.56,.59,.56))
for n, size, pos in [
    ('SinkFrontLip',(.62,.018,.018),(sx,sy-.195,1.074)),
    ('SinkRearLip',(.62,.018,.018),(sx,sy+.195,1.074)),
    ('SinkLeftLip',(.018,.39,.018),(sx-.31,sy,1.074)),
    ('SinkRightLip',(.018,.39,.018),(sx+.31,sy,1.074))]:
    block(island,n,size,pos,(.76,.78,.74))
faucet_pts = [(sx+.20,sy+.27,1.06),(sx+.20,sy+.27,1.27),
              (sx+.18,sy+.25,1.31),(sx+.12,sy+.18,1.32),
              (sx+.07,sy+.10,1.30),(sx+.07,sy+.07,1.25)]
island.include('Faucet', sweep_tube(points=faucet_pts, radius=.012, color=(.65,.69,.68)))
island.include('TapLever', rod(.008, start=(sx+.25,sy+.27,1.09),
                             end=(sx+.28,sy+.27,1.17), color=(.65,.69,.68)))
scene.include('Island', island)

hood = Asset('SuspendedHood')
block(hood, 'HoodBody', (1.00,.94,HOOD_TOP-HOOD_BOTTOM),
      (.15,.20,(HOOD_TOP+HOOD_BOTTOM)/2), (.73,.73,.67))
block(hood, 'BottomPlate', (.97,.91,.025), (.15,.20,HOOD_BOTTOM), (.54,.56,.52))
block(hood, 'GreaseFilter', (.68,.56,.008), (.15,.20,HOOD_BOTTOM-.017), (.37,.39,.36))
for i in range(2):
    block(hood, 'UnderLamp_%d'%i, (.055,.07,.009),
          (-.16+i*.60,-.12,HOOD_BOTTOM-.021), (.85,.86,.75))
scene.include('SuspendedHood', hood)

kitchen = Asset('RearCabinetry')
# Left tall cabinet is strongly cropped and partially hidden by the foreground post.
block(kitchen, 'LeftTallCabinet', (.84,.73,2.66), (-1.87,1.46,1.33), black)
block(kitchen, 'LeftTallDoor', (.81,.025,2.59), (-1.87,1.08,1.34), (.039,.046,.043))
block(kitchen, 'TallUpperSeam', (.80,.012,.009), (-1.87,1.061,2.31), (.019,.023,.021))
block(kitchen, 'BackBase', (3.10,.65,.94), (-.08,1.58,.47), (.025,.030,.027))
block(kitchen, 'BackCounter', (3.12,.70,.045), (-.08,1.53,.965), (.16,.18,.16))
for i in range(5):
    block(kitchen, 'BaseDoor_%d'%i, (.60,.025,.80),
          (-1.30+i*.62,1.241,.47), (.036,.043,.039))
block(kitchen, 'Backsplash', (3.15,.055,.86), (-.06,1.92,1.40), (.069,.080,.069))
for i in range(5):
    block(kitchen, 'BacksplashJoint_%d'%i, (.008,.006,.83),
          (-1.5+i*.63,1.888,1.40), (.036,.045,.039))
block(kitchen, 'UpperCabinet', (3.12,.52,.61), (-.08,1.77,2.13), (.055,.064,.057))
block(kitchen, 'UpperSoffit', (3.13,.55,.035), (-.08,1.75,1.81), (.022,.028,.023))
block(kitchen, 'WarmRecessPanel', (2.03,.018,.37), (-.45,1.865,1.23), (.31,.26,.23))
block(kitchen, 'LightStrip', (2.04,.025,.013), (-.45,1.80,1.425), (.95,.79,.57))
# Small red appliance is a conspicuous spot in the otherwise neutral niche.
block(kitchen, 'CoffeeMachineFoot', (.20,.16,.025), (.00,1.60,.99), (.018,.02,.018))
kitchen.include('RedCoffeeMachine', ball(.091, center=(.00,1.64,1.105), color=(.68,.008,.019)))
block(kitchen, 'CoffeeMachineFace', (.12,.025,.13), (.00,1.554,1.095), (.025,.029,.027))
scene.include('RearCabinetry', kitchen)

ovens = Asset('OvenTower')
block(ovens, 'TowerBody', (.80,.77,2.51), (1.91,1.55,1.255), (.034,.042,.038))
block(ovens, 'RightSurround', (.19,.85,2.75), (2.40,1.56,1.375), (.046,.054,.048))
block(ovens, 'TowerUpperDoor', (.75,.025,.65), (1.91,1.15,2.15), (.032,.039,.035))
for i, z in enumerate([1.04,1.55]):
    block(ovens, 'OvenFrame_%d'%i, (.66,.045,.455), (1.91,1.135,z), (.25,.28,.27))
    block(ovens, 'OvenGlass_%d'%i, (.58,.018,.315), (1.91,1.105,z-.025), (.023,.043,.048))
    block(ovens, 'ControlBar_%d'%i, (.64,.025,.065), (1.91,1.093,z+.173), (.34,.36,.34))
    block(ovens, 'OvenHandle_%d'%i, (.52,.045,.022), (1.91,1.066,z+.10), (.52,.55,.53))
block(ovens, 'LowerDoor', (.75,.035,.73), (1.91,1.14,.38), (.04,.047,.042))
block(ovens, 'RightWallReturn', (.55,.17,3.0), (2.65,2.02,1.5), (.39,.42,.39))
scene.include('OvenTower', ovens)

sc = bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('AmbientWorld')
sc.world.use_nodes = True
sc.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs['Color'].default_value = (.50,.55,.59,1)
sc.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs['Strength'].default_value = .23

# Fine grain and surface variation are procedural, avoiding decorative mesh fields.
def descendants(group):
    ob = bpy.data.objects.get(group)
    return [q for q in ob.children_recursive if q.type == 'MESH'] if ob else []

woodmat = bpy.data.materials.new('Natural vertical oak')
woodmat.use_nodes = True
nt = woodmat.node_tree
bs = nt.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = .53
tex = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
tex.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 3.8
tex.inputs['Detail'].default_value = 3.5
coord = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
mapping = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath')
mapping.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
mapping.inputs[1].default_value = (9,9,.35)
nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Generated'],mapping.inputs[0])
nt.links.new(mapping.outputs['Vector'],tex.inputs['Vector'])
ramp = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position = .18
ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (.12,.065,.028,1)
ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position = .82
ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (.53,.34,.18,1)
nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],ramp.inputs[0])
nt.links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'],bs.inputs['Base Color'])
bump = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBump')
bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value = .16
bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value = .025
nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height'])
nt.links.new(bump.outputs[0],bs.inputs['Normal'])
for ob in descendants('TimberColumns'):
    ob.data.materials.clear()
    ob.data.materials.append(woodmat)

for mat in bpy.data.materials:
    if mat.use_nodes:
        shader = mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
        if shader and mat != woodmat:
            shader.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = .44

for ob in descendants('Island'):
    if 'Faucet' in ob.name or 'Tap' in ob.name:
        for mat in ob.data.materials:
            if mat.use_nodes:
                p = mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
